Introduce harsher sentencing for theft and fund increased police presence, We think the government should introduce harsher sentencing for theft. We also think more police should be patrolling on our streets., We think more police could tackle incidents of public theft with regards to shoplifting and increasing phone theft, ensuring criminals are held accountable for their actions.
 
There has been a rise in people stealing from shops and pickpocketing and we think this has caused local communities to become unsafe.

Ban the suffering, fast-growing 'frankenchicken' breeds, I think a lot of the chicken sold in the UK comes from unethical, overcrowded chicken farms that develop fast growing chicken breeds, otherwise known as 'Frankenchickens'., The reason that I think these farms are unethical is because I believe the chickens live a life of suffering as they have been modified to eat unnatural quantities of food to fuel their fast growth. This can lead to many problems, including their inability to walk and often laying in their own waste. The thing that angers me most is that I think most people have no awareness of this issue and continue to buy cheap chicken that had been raised in what I think is a disgraceful way.

Introduce Licensing for Mobile Phones to Prevent Scams and Protect Consumers, Introduce a licensing system for all mobile phones in the UK, including contract and pay-as-you-go devices. Require phones to be verified and linked to an account holder, ensuring they are genuine, secure, and preventing counterfeit phones from being used to steal users’ personal data., Counterfeit mobile phones are being sold as genuine on social media, online marketplaces, and second-hand websites. Once connected to the home internet, these devices can steal personal data and passwords without the buyer’s knowledge, similar to a Trojan Horse virus that copies the user's keyboard input unbeknown to the buyer.  We think a licensing system would verify devices and link them to account holders, protecting consumers, reducing cybercrime, and enhancing mobile security in today's tech world.

Introduce measures to address longevity and repair of products, Introduce measures addressing longevity and repair of products, including:
 
- requiring companies to provide repair manuals and spare parts
 
- requiring manufacturers to consider longevity in product design
 
- encouraging companies to promote sustainable consumption, I think it will help tackle 'planned obsolescence', the practice of designing products to become obsolete or non-functional after a certain period, which in my view often leads to higher consumer spending and environmental waste.
 
I would like to see measures to encourage durable, repairable products, promoting sustainable consumption, holding corporations to account for manufacturing practices.
 
I think ending planned obsolescence will promote a more eco-friendly and consumer-centric market.

Give automatic equal benefits rights to separated parents who are co-parenting, It's 2025. Many couples do not stay in relationships like our grandparents or ancestors used to. If parents are amicable, we think that each parent should get equal rights to housing, benefits and support., We think the government need to change the current rules and that child benefit should be shared if parents are co-parenting in a 50/50 agreement.
 
Currently, the parent in receipt of child benefit gets prioritised for social housing and the other parent is classed as a single person and of lesser priority. The "single" person also wouldn't be granted additional bedrooms when applying for social housing.

Ban junk mail generically addressed to "The Occupier", "The Householder" etc, Please ban these addressed forms of junk mail now, i.e. mail addressed to generic addressees (e.g. The Occupier) where no commercial relationship is already in place., Unsubscribing (Royal Mail Door to Door opt out, MPS (Mail Preference Service), and DMA's "Your Choice" scheme) do nothing, because these mailings have an "addressee" on them.
 
We think these unwanted mailings are a complete waste of paper and irritating to many people. Many people didn't ask for them, but have to deal with them. We think producing them may also add extra cost to the products and services we buy, because companies may include the cost of producing junk mail into the prices we pay.

Review process for Foster Carers transferring between local authorities, The current process expects you to be reassessed when you move local authority. Foster Carers are assessed at a professional level and we think should be able to easily move Counties should they wish., Many Councils are desperate for Foster Carers. We think the current transfer process for existing, approved carers is difficult and complicated, creating a barrier which prevents good quality carers wanting to move from one area to another. Once approved and are subject to continual Supervision, checks and training. Why do they need to go through the reassessment process from scratch? We think it is unnecessary and unwarranted.

Stop taxis operating outside their licensing area, Taxis operating outside their licensing area (cross-border taxis) can create challenges for commuters, operators, and drivers. We believe they disrupt the transport system, causing unfair competition and confusion. As a driver, I’ve seen the frustration and income losses caused by this practice. , Cross-border private hire drivers operating outside their licensing authority area can disrupt local transport and cause income losses. We believe they exploit regulatory loopholes, poaching fares without necessarily meeting local rules. We think this undermines public safety, drivers’ livelihoods, and trust in the system. We urge the government to develop stricter regulations and close these loopholes to protect hardworking local drivers and ensure a fair, safe, and reliable transport system for all.

Increase funding for people with Parkinson’s and implement the "Parky Charter", We want the government to take the decisive five steps set out in the Movers and Shakers' "Parky Charter" and to fulfil the Health Secretary’s promises. , As a priority, we want to make sure that everyone referred for a possible Parkinson’s diagnosis sees a consultant within 18 weeks and at least once a year after that.
 
As set out in the Parky Charter, we want:
 
1. Speedy specialists
2. Instant information
3. Parkinson's passport
4. Comprehensive care
5. Quest for a cure
 
Parkinson’s is considered the fastest growing neurological condition in the world. We think it’s time for the government to respond to our grave concerns about what we consider systematic failings in Parkinson’s care.
 
The measures in the Parky Charter, which are supported by the three big Parkinson’s charities, require the government to deliver on their promises, ensuring timely diagnosis, comprehensive care, and dignity for all people with Parkinson’s.

Require councils to give everyone a month off of paying council tax, We want the government to give everyone a month off from paying council tax. We are concerned that there are potholes on the roads, roads have been left ungritted and household waste has sometimes not been collected., We pay council tax for the council to do things. We feel that their obligations have not been met.

Require schools to allow students to use their phones at break and lunch, We think that students should be allowed to use their phones during break and lunch because it provides them with the opportunity to connect with people. Phones can allow students to stay in touch with family and friends, access helpful resources, and arrange group activities., Students could also use apps for relaxation, creativity, or even catching up on homework. We think that allowing responsible phone use fosters trust and teaches time management, preparing students for the real world where technology could be essential.

Amend the Health and Safety Act to make mental health training mandatory, We urge the Government to amend the Health and Safety Act to require all workplaces to provide mandatory mental health awareness training, to ensure that mental health is given the same priority as physical health and safety, helping to create healthier and more productive work environments., We believe this would lead to:
 
Improved Employee Well-being: A proactive approach to mental health can reduce stress, anxiety, and burnout.
Economic Gains: Supporting mental health can lower absenteeism and presenteeism, saving businesses money.
Equal Priority: Mental health training would ensure mental health is treated with the same seriousness as fire safety and other physical health risks.

Make it illegal for the media to shame victims of romance fraud, We believe it should be illegal for the media to use victim-shaming language in their headlines and news reports. We think that doing so is secondary victimisation, which includes harassment and discrimination, that the media should be held accountable for., Romance fraud destroys lives. It is a cruel and devastating crime where fraudsters groom victims through coercive control, similar to domestic abuse.
 
However, we think that sections of the British press believe that victims of romance fraud are legitimate targets for ridicule. We believe this is completely unethical and this pure form of victim shaming will stop others coming forward to report crimes. We do not think that victims should have to live with the shame they are made to feel.

Create an inclusive special envoy for home educating families, Create a special envoy for home educating families, who would be a mediator between Government, officials and the Home Education Community, and suggest amendments to the Children’s Wellbeing & Schools Bill. This special envoy should include home educating parents. , We think this would benefit home educated children who we want to achieve their best potential.
 
We think Part 2, Sections 25 - 30 of the Children’s Wellbeing & Schools Bill is not fit for purpose in its present state and should be amended because we think it:
- is poorly researched, lacks understanding of home education, may put additional children at risk, especially those from families who have experienced Domestic Violence or Child Abuse.
- is ambiguous, lacks straightforwardness and simplicity which may lend it easily to misuse of power.
- undermines children's rights as protected in UNCRC.

Add the subject of post-partum mental illness to the national curriculum, Outline post partum depression, and other mental illnesses that can happen before, during and after pregnancy/birth. We think this could happen either at the end of sex education talks or through mental health awareness talks., We believe this could help reduce maternal suicide rates as suicide continues to be the leading cause of direct maternal death between 6 weeks and 12 months post partum. To help ensure all women can access the help they need and not feel ashamed. To raise awareness of this and to educate pupils on signs and symptoms, where to go for help, which services would help and lessen the burden and worry on new parents. We think this could improve the quality of life for families and keep new mums and babies as safe as possible.

Fund improvements for young people with SEND who visit GP surgeries, I want the government to require GP surgeries to offer priority appointments and home visits for children and young adults with special educational needs and disabilities who are unable to access a surgery easily., I also want the government to fund GP surgeries to have calming areas or sensory rooms available for children and young adults to access when they are able to visit a surgery.

Hold parents legally accountable for their children’s actions, I believe parents should be held accountable, alongside their children, in a court of law for their children's actions. Parents should not be able to abdicate their responsibilities for their child's actions., I believe parents have a duty to educate, act as role model and bring their children up as decent law-abiding citizens. I believe too many young people are committing serious crimes, but are not always tried in adult courts, and parents appear to have no responsibility for the children or their actions and abdicate themselves from their responsibilities as parents.

More direct communication between the NHS and the Government & Parliament, We want the Government and Parliament to have more communication with frontline NHS workers like nurses. This could include monthly NHS video calls from each county in England to work out what is needed., We think better communication between the staff who do the practical work and the government could help them establish a better allocation of resources in each separate county.
 
To improve communication, the government could speak directly to staff about current issues. They could have monthly video calls with staff in different areas to improve patient care and reduce hospital stay duration.

Provide funding to increase police presence on the streets, We want more funding to increase police presence on our streets. We think that police need to be seen daily, as a non-threatening but quiet and reassuring presence. We feel that knife crime is out of control, there is a general feeling of unease and a lack of safety in our society., We feel that a police presence on our streets would bring a feeling of order back to our daily lives. We want our families and everyone in our country to have that sense of being supported and protected. We feel like we are on our own right now dealing with feeling unsafe situations outside and it’s not good enough.

Increase funding for ARFID treatment, We think that everyone who needs it should be able to access treatment for ARFID. I think funding should be increased for the treatment of ARFID., We demand that the Eating Disorder Services be inclusive of ARFID - as should be the basic human right of anyone suffering. We believe too many people are falling through the cracks in the system. We believe that ARFID individuals deserve equal rights to treatment and the chance to recover from this life-threatening disorder.

Fund a full bursary and maintenance fund to train Learning Disability Nurses, At a time when the demand across health and social care is so high, numbers entering the LD nursing profession are too low. To halt this decline, support the profession with a full bursary and maintenance fund. Now is time for action., Learning Disability Nursing has adapted over the years and LDNs have been instrumental in the shift to independent community living. LDNs now work in all areas of health and social care supporting individuals with disabilities to access specialist support. Unfortunately the numbers of universities offering the course and the numbers of students selecting the course has fallen to unsustainable levels. Historically many were mature students who now find it unaffordable.

Put education on allergy & autoimmune based diets on the National Curriculum, Introduce into the national curriculum information about food allergies and celiac disease with emphasis on their severity and impact on the functioning of sufferers., We believe that misinformation surrounding celiac disease in particular is rife and growing, with recent articles citing it as a “fad”. In order to ensure sufferers are well supported we think mass education is essential. We think that ensuring awareness from a young age promotes understanding towards peers and develops general understanding of the severity of dietary requirements.

More funding for GPs to provide face-to-face appointments and walk-in clinics, I would like the Government to increase funding to GPs to help ensure they provide face-to-face appointments for everyone who wants them, and increase walk-in clinics so everyone is able to more easily walk in and see doctors rather than potentially just being offered telephone calls., I would like this to happen so people can see a doctor in person, explain their conditions to them and have the doctor assess them in person rather than just speaking over the phone.
 
A face-to-face appointment could help many people a lot more than a mere phone call.

Fund more A&E services, I would like the Government to provide more funding for more 24 hour A&E services and reopening local A&E departments that have been closed, to help waiting times come down., I would like this funding to be used to reopen closed A&E departments, such as the one at Trafford General Hospital, so people don’t have to travel further in an emergency.

DON'T extend the BBC Licence fee to Streaming Services like Netflix & Disney+., Do not extend the BBC Licence Fee to include streaming service subscriptions such as Netflix and Disney+ as there are many UK residents moving away from BBC TV, Radio and streaming service for alternative providers., It has been reported that the Labour government could extend the TV Licence to streaming service subscriptions such as Netflix and Disney+. Many UK residents are switching to these alternative entertainment services as they often provide better content. It would be unfair to force people to pay into an organisation for a service that they do not use. We believe that we should have the right to choose our entertainment provider.

Ban the residential use of artificial grass, We urge the Government to introduce a ban on both the use and sale of artificial grass in residential settings. This should include prohibiting its installation in private gardens and outdoor spaces, as well as restricting retailers from selling it for domestic use., Artificial grass harms the environment by destroying habitats and contributing to plastic pollution, and may increase flood risk. It can displace plants that absorb carbon, and kill soil life, and offers no support for pollinators. It can prevent absorption of rainwater. It degrades into microplastics, polluting waterways and harming wildlife. It also retains heat, which may contribute to urban areas experiencing higher temperatures. We believe a ban would protect biodiversity, reduce pollution, and promote sustainable landscaping.

Allow care workers to bring their families to the UK, We want the government to allow care workers to bring their families to the UK on their visa. We think this is vital for the hearts and souls of carers. This could reduce the emotional and mental health impacts of separation and stop carers from being isolated., Keeping families together is a lifeline for some. Some parents who work as carers are living with the pain of separation. Children have been separated from their parents and they are living without their warmth and touch, miles away. We feel that families should never be torn apart when love and unity are what heal the most.

Require airlines to provide/sell sanitary products, We want the government to require in law for airlines to provide/sell sanitary products., People who menstruate consist of half of our population, and many people who menstruate know that one's cycle is not always predictable. Experiencing an unexpected period whilst flying can happen quite frequently, and due to a general lack of awareness, I feel this has not been addressed. For better inclusivity and general care for passengers' health, I think such a law is necessary to be made.

Legislate for Mobile Phones to have Hardware "Kill Switch" to help reduce thefts, To legislate to require all mobile phones imported into, or manufactured in the UK, to have a Hardware Kill switch. This would prevent stolen phones from being accessed by the thieves. We believe current software security does not provide adequate protection., According to figures from the Metropolitan Police, 70,137 phones were stolen in London in 2024. 
 
Mobile phone theft can cause dramatic trauma to the victim, and is a major crime wave. Information yielded from the phone can be used to fraudulently extort money from bank accounts, and the phones are reprogrammed and sold on the black market.

Unban the supply of plastic straws, stirrers and cotton buds, The ban on plastic straws, drink stirrers and cotton buds was introduced to reduce plastic waste, but I think it has unintended consequences. For some disabled individuals, plastic straws are preferable to alternatives such as paper or metal., I think the ban on plastic straws, drink stirrers and cotton buds fails to address the major sources of plastic pollution. I think more should be done to target industrial sources and discarded fishing gear, rather than focussing on everyday consumer items.

Change child maintenance liability so it's not based on income, We think there should be set a minimum Child Maintenance which is minimum amount needed for child care eg. £100 a week. Where a child is cared by single parent the other should pay 50% of this amount. Being jailed or student should not be exempt from liability - like with a joint mortgage., Child rising costs are high. No parent should be exempt from participating. Joint mortgage is shared responsibility regardless if couple split, child maintenance should have the same principle. The wellbeing of the child, human life should have priority over property in UK.

Review and change regulations on gambling advertisements., I want the regulations regarding gambling advertising to be reviewed and changed to restrict the times they're shown and the frequency.
Seeing these adverts on TV constantly is demoralizing and it is no wonder we have a gambling crisis.
Why endure a slew of gambling ads back-to-back on daytime TV?, The Government identifies gambling as a national issue contributing to the mental health crisis. Despite this, gambling adverts are prominently repeated and shown during daytime TV.
This exposure exacerbates addiction struggles and related mental health issues, costing the nation millions annually. And we wonder why there is a crisis?
Stricter regulation of gambling advertisements is essential to mitigate the negative impact of gambling and support those affected.

TV shouldn't push gambling.

Build Specialist Emergency Care Hospital in Sutton & invest in Epsom & St.Helier, Immediately fully fund the Building Your Future Hospitals programme delivering a new Specialist Emergency Care Hospital in Sutton and invest in Epsom and St Helier hospitals before they fall down, St Helier hospital is falling down and health provision is failing in Epsom and St Helier

Require all Family Law Professionals to have training on neurodivergence , I urge the government to make mandatory neurodivergent training a requirement for all family law professionals. This training should focus on understanding neurodivergence, recognising abuse in neurodivergent survivors, & providing tailored support to ensure fair and just treatment in family courts., We believe the unique needs of neurodivergent individuals, especially survivors of domestic abuse, are not currently well understood by professionals in the family law system. This training could help to:

Improve understanding of neurodivergent conditions (such as ASD & ADHD) & their impact.
Recognise signs of abuse in neurodivergent individuals.
Provide appropriate communication strategies & reasonable accommodations.
Ensure that neurodivergent survivors receive fair treatment and have access to justice.

Strengthen laws on Phone Theft & stolen data, Introduce harsher punishments for phone theft, regardless of the perpetrator’s age. Recognize the loss of software, data, and personal information as a significant factor in legal proceedings.
Classify the theft and misuse of personal data from stolen devices as a specific offence., According to the recent crime statistics, phone theft has surged, particularly in urban areas.
Many thefts can involve violence or intimidation, making it a serious safety concern.
Phones are stolen and quickly resold or stripped for parts, creating a lucrative criminal industry.
Personal and sensitive data (bank details, photos, private communications) can often be compromised.
Victims can suffer emotional distress, privacy violations, and financial risks (such as fraud or identity theft).

Strengthen laws ensuring Banks report Blackmail & Money Laundering, We believe stricter anti-money laundering measures are needed to ensure Banks are held accountable and are actively identifying and reporting suspicious financial activity linked to blackmail and coercion. , We believe that Institutions that fail to act should face penalties for their negligence. We believe major banks in England and Wales have ignored clear cases of blackmail and money laundering, allowing criminals to exploit victims. We believe banks have failed to report suspicious activity through Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs), leaving victims unprotected. I urge Parliament to put forward stricter AML laws, hold banks accountable, and protect victims from financial coercion. We think stronger oversight, penalties for negligence, and victim support systems are essential. The Government must act now.

Regulate Sodium Nitrite & Improve Mental Health Services to Prevent Suicides, 1. Introduce strict regulations on the sale of sodium nitrite to prevent misuse.
2. Work with online retailers to restrict access to highly concentrated forms.
3. Fund Improved NHS mental health crisis responses, ensuring safeguarding measures when individuals disclose access to lethal substances., Sodium nitrite is a highly toxic substance that is easily purchased online. It can be used for suicide. Despite its known dangers, it remains widely available with minimal regulation.

We want action to prevent further avoidable deaths.

We think the government should introduce legislation restricting the sale of sodium nitrite. NHS mental health services should be funded to implement stricter safeguarding policies, ensuring immediate action when individuals disclose access to lethal substances.

Review Section 91(14) orders, The Government should review section 91(14) of the Children Act 1989. Consider stricter criteria of when barring orders under the section can be used. We think these orders could affect a child’s wellbeing and the voice of the child and parent., We think when safeguarding concerns are raised, the order should cease immediately. We believe any judge considering making such orders should be required to have a fact-finding hearing as a standard first.

Base Extended Producer Responsibility fees for packaging on units not weight, In its current format, the EPR regulations disproportionately impact businesses using glass. We think the regulations should be changed from a weight-based fee structure to a unit-based one to help towards the UK's Net Zero Goals., The weight-based fee structure disproportionately impacts businesses using glass despite it being one of the most sustainable and safest packaging materials available.
We believe the current EPR model:
- Drives up costs for businesses and consumers during a cost-of-living crisis
- Pushes companies to switch to less sustainable materials
- Gives an advantage to imported glass with higher carbon footprints

Require schools to ban students use of smartphones during school hours, We want the Government to introduce a policy that requires schools to ban smartphones during school hours, including break time. We think this could help ensure a focused and productive learning environment., We feel that while smartphones offer benefits like communication and access to educational tools, they also pose challenges in schools.
We believe that many students use phones for non-educational purposes, which can disrupt learning, and contribute to issues like cyberbullying and social pressure, impacting mental health.
Families may not always be aware of what is being shared by children. Once posted, content may not be fully erased, leaving digital footprints that can affect their reputation and opportunities into adulthood.

Legislate against MPs receiving public funds if convicted, We want the Government to legislate against MPs accessing or receiving public funds while serving any type of sentence, suspended or custodial, as we think this would bring their office into disrepute.

We feel that on moral standing, this rule is incompatible with the Public's expectations.,

Demand Stronger Sentences for Domestic Abusers to Ensure Justice for Victims, To review and revamp sentences for convicted domestic abusers. Current penalties are too lenient and fail to reflect the severity of the crimes or the lasting trauma victims endure. Increased sentencing is necessary to properly address these heinous acts and their devastating impact on the victims., Domestic abuse victims often feel unheard, unsupported, and powerless to report their abusers due to the leniency in the current sentencing system. In a recent Edinburgh case, a victim endured 10 years of abuse, escalating to attempted murder, yet the abuser received a minimum sentence of just 7 years. This is not justice. Longer sentences will send a clear message to abusers and demonstrate that the courts and government are committed to supporting victims and holding perpetrators accountable.

Make an agreed offer on a property legally binding, I want the government to legislate to change the point at which there is a binding contract during house sales. Once an offer has been agreed, I think here should be a financial penalty for pulling out of the contract., When buyers withdraw from property sales without warning, it can cost people money.

Require schools to display school meal nutritional information, Require all UK schools to display full nutritional data for every meal served, in addition to allergen information. We think this should include:
Calories
Vitamin and mineral content
Macronutrients
Sugar, salt, and saturated fat content
Ingredient sourcing, We think parents, students, and school staff deserve clear information about what children are eating.
With over 25% of UK children overweight or obese, we think transparency would help promote healthier eating habits.
Supporting Special Dietary Needs: Many students have allergies, intolerances, or medical conditions that require specific nutritional management.
Encouraging Schools to Improve Standards: When meal data is visible, we think there is a greater incentive for schools to offer nutritious, balanced options.

Allocate funding to allow unpaid carers one night off, Allocate funding so that unpaid carers can have at least one night off per month. This will help prevent burnout and job losses among carers who suffer extreme sleep deprivation while they care for loved ones., I believe chronic sleep deprivation is a daily reality for many unpaid carers and contributes to burnout. With respite care often costing more than £100 per night and Carers Allowance at just £83.30 per week, which barely covers the rising living costs, I believe more funding is needed to help carers have a proper rest while caring.

Legislate to require tech companies to offer parental controls for under 17's, We urge the UK Government to require tech companies to offer parental controls for all users under 17, based on agreed standards. These controls should, at a minimum, manage screen time, app use, and content access., Some tech companies allow children to disable parental controls at 13, and no regulations set clear standards for tech companies. I believe unrestricted digital access can negatively affect mental health, development, and learning. I believe standardised, reliable parental controls would help protect children, support parents, and foster healthier digital habits into adulthood.

Reinstate the Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) to support farmers and nature, Reinstate the Sustainable Farming Incentive (SFI) to help farmers transition to regenerative agriculture, improve soil health, protect biodiversity, and strengthen UK food security. We believe that this scheme for sustainable farming and nature recovery was cut without warning, putting this at risk., The SFI supported farmers in restoring degraded soil, reducing pollution, sequestering carbon, and enhancing biodiversity while ensuring economic viability. We think its removal undermines farmers, food security, and climate resilience, placing the UK’s legally binding Net Zero target in jeopardy. At COP28, nations committed to transitioning 160M hectares to regenerative agriculture by 2030. We believe that without SFI we are regressing and failing all points.

Mobile Phone Control for 16 and under
 ., No mobile phones until you are 16. No Social media until you are 16. More phone boxes outside and inside schools for ringing in routine calls / emergency 
 ., No mobile phones until you are 16. No Social media until you are 16. More phone boxes outside and inside schools for ringing in routine calls / emergency 
 .

Introduce mandatory anti-bullying programmes in schools, I urge the Government to introduce mandatory anti-bullying education programmes in schools. These programmes should promote awareness, provide support, and create safe environments for students, helping them understand the importance of kindness and tackling bullying., Bullying is a widespread issue and can affect students' well-being and academic success. By introducing mandatory anti-bullying education programmes, we can create a supportive environment where young people feel safe, understood, and empowered to seek help. Early intervention and awareness may reduce stigma, promote emotional resilience, and prevent long-term consequences, ultimately fostering a healthier, more inclusive society for future generations.

Raise the minimum legal age to make adult content to 25, We think the minimum age to become a content creator in the adult industry should be raised to 25 to protect the welfare of young adults., We feel that young people are vulnerable and should be protected from getting into this line of work at such an early age. We have heard stories being revealed, predominately about young females, who have admitted to getting involved in situations that they regret or struggled to get out of. We think the modern day headlines are becoming a danger to society by glamorising the industry as a way to make 'quick and easy money' and target those who are not old enough to understand the potential consequences.

Advise the Commonwealth not to grant membership to the USA, Reports indicate the US is interested in joining the Commonwealth. We think the British Government should advise against this as we think the current US administration’s actions & statements are not compatible with the principles in the Commonwealth Charter., We think principles 4,6,7,9 and 10 of the Commonwealth Charter are incompatible with current US policy, and consider that this is evidenced by statements and actions taken since January 20th.
 
We think US policy around diversity does not express tolerance or understanding. We think tariffs work against the flow of trade on equitable terms. We think withdrawal from international agreements on climate change is not a commitment to collective action.

Protect consumers from cosmetic surgery financial scams, We call on the Government to introduce stronger regulations to protect consumers from cosmetic surgery scams. We believe many patients may have lost money to companies that take upfront payments, cancel procedures, and then go into liquidation—while directors recover their funds first., To prevent this, we urge the Government to:
• Require payments to be held in an escrow account until the procedure takes place, ensuring funds are protected.
• Enforce stricter financial oversight of cosmetic surgery providers to stop directors from prioritizing their own funds over patients. 
• Introduce tougher penalties for companies engaging in unethical financial practices.
 
We think these changes could protect consumers from financial loss and prevent businesses from exploiting vulnerable patients.

Offer a free app to children and parents that monitors and manages their phones, The UK Prime Minister has spoken out about phone use in children. He should now ensure that in the UK all parents/carers are offered a free app that monitors, manages and regulates their child's phone usage. All parents of under 16 year olds should have access to this technology., There are a number of apps and tech platforms that can be installed on parent/carers and children/teens phones that help the parents manage their internet access, phone time and enables parents to set boundaries for phone use. This technology isn't known about by everyone and comes at a cost. Given we are on the cusp of a global smart phone crisis with children and teens accessing everything on the internet, the Government should be taking action by creating / offering a tool like this for all.

Fair funding for Early Years Care: To allow quality, training, and transparency, 1. Increase, publish and properly allocate funding to match the actual cost of delivery
2. Funding to support, train and retain skilled early years professionals
3. Allow providers to charge fair fees if funding doesn't meet the cost of delivery, Help equal access to high quality early education for all. 

We believe:
• Parents deserve clear, honest information about how much funding is provided by the government
• Early years providers need sustainable funding that reflects the true cost of delivering quality care, paying fair wages, and maintaining safe, nurturing environments.
• Children deserve access to high-quality early education that supports their development, well-being, and future success

We think our children deserve quality, parents deserve transparency, providers deserve sustainability.

Add Assault of a Roadworker to the Crime and Policing Bill, The Crime and Policing Bill, includes a specific new offence of assaulting retail workers. Given the increasing levels of abuse, verbal and physical, towards road workers and we think they should be added to the legislation., No one should go to work and suffer abuse by doing their job, 1 in 4 road workers suffer abuse regularly, and we think this could be higher as it goes unreported as they believe nothing can or will be done. We think this is not acceptable and there needs to be consequences this occurs, we need to ensure that there is also more awareness around this.

Department for Education fund to improve mental health services in all schools, We want the Government to increase funding for mental health services in all schools, ensuring that every student has access to professional support. This includes hiring more school counsellors, funding mental health training for staff, and integrating mental health education into the curriculum., Mental health issues among students are rising, with anxiety, depression, and stress affecting their well-being and academic performance. Many schools lack the resources to provide adequate support, leaving students without the help they need. Increased government funding would ensure every school can offer professional mental health services, helping students cope with challenges and succeed in their education.

Phase out and ban the sale of plastic manual toothbrushes by 2040, We urge the Government to ban plastic manual toothbrushes by 2040 through a phased out plan. This includes restricting sales, supporting eco-friendly alternatives, running awareness campaigns and enforcing legislation to reduce plastic waste and protect the environment., By working together, we think we can reduce plastic waste and ensure a sustainable future.

Make neurodiversity training mandatory for all education staff, We want the government to introduce mandatory neurodiversity training for all teachers and support staff as part of core training., We think this will help tackle inaccessible education, improve inclusion for neurodivergent pupils, and reduce mental health risks through better understanding, early support, and inclusive practices.
 
Many neurodivergent pupils face barriers in school due to a lack of understanding and support. Only 14% of secondary school teachers have received more than half a day’s training on autism, and autistic pupils are twice as likely to be excluded. We believe this contributes to poor mental health and emotional distress.
 
Mandatory training could help staff create inclusive classrooms, recognise distress early, make reasonable adjustments, and ensure neurodivergent children feel safe, supported, and able to thrive.

Revoke The Selective Licensing of Houses (Additional Conditions) Order 2015, We think the Selective Licensing of Houses (Additional Conditions) (England) Order 2015 should be revoked immediately by the Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government and not implement new schemes or renew any schemes currently in effect., We think this order is insidious. We think Councils may use it to implement heavy-handed measures where communities are most diverse without consideration for sensitivities of minority groups.
 
We think the Renters Rights Bill provides for a Private Rented Sector database obviating a need for such schemes.

Ban Child Abuse Activist Groups live streaming content, We think Organised Child Abuse Activist Groups should be banned from live streaming content. These activist groups may engage in communication with adults online and imitate being a child. 
, They may also live stream on social media the suspects home address, pre investigation/charge which we think puts many at risk of harm.

We think the issue with OCAGs posting and live streaming a suspects location, home address and name, as well as there image causes many safeguarding concerns. First of all, an investigation has not been carried out, the suspect identified by the OCAG group may be completely innocent, and we think it impacts a fair trial. We think it may also put family members, including children at the addresses at risk of harm from other vigilante groups.

Ban printer companies from disabling ink after subscription ends, Make it illegal for printer manufacturers to remotely deactivate ink cartridges after a subscription ends. We think ink that has been paid for and is still functional should remain usable regardless of subscription status., We think this practice is wasteful, anti-consumer, and environmentally irresponsible. We think it means users may have to discard usable ink and buy more unnecessarily. We think consumers may be subjected to hidden costs for essential printing functions in homes and businesses.

Ban parents from using their children to create social media content, We want the government to bring in legislation to protect children used by parents for content creation. We think this could protect them from abuse, exploitation and exposure to paedophiles., We think some parents are clearly exploiting their children for financial benefit and using inappropriate photos of them on video thumbnails most likely to gain views.

25% reduction in council tax for those living alone is not enough, It carries the assumption that 4 adults live in each house.
Each person is a burden to services, (potholes, fire prevention, libraries, police, etc) not each household. Council tax should be per person not per house., It should not be up to each council, but decided by the government. Council tax is used to pay for local services and repairs, like waste disposal, libraries and education, police and fire departments, transport and highways and so on.
Also, single people don't put the bin out each time there is a collection if not full.
Single people, widowed, etc should not have to pay a higher amount than other people. The reduction should be 50% as a min. It should be paid by every adult not every house.

Review and strengthen mandatory allergy training for all food industry staff, We want the Government to review and strengthen allergy training for all food industry staff, including front-of-house and kitchen roles, to ensure safe handling, clear communication, and better protection for allergy sufferers., We want to make the UK safer for allergy sufferers. Over 2 million people in the UK have food allergies, and even tiny traces can trigger severe or life-threatening reactions. We believe that improving the training staff receive would raise awareness, reduce risks, and help prevent future tragedies.

Specialist Hospital Units for Vulnerable Young Adults with learning disabilities, Fund specialist hospital units for young adults with learning disabilities and additional needs, including autism, which offer them paediatric care to age 18 where clinically appropriate. The units should be sensory-considerate, ease the eventual transition to adult care and minimise distress., We would also like parents or carers to be able to remain in the units 24/7, and for consistent, inclusive, compassionate care to be ensured across all NHS hospitals.

We think care decisions should be based on developmental rather than chronological age, with an emphasis on individual needs.

We believe these young people deserve care that respects their unique challenges. We think they need understanding, not assumptions. We think they need protection, not policies that in our view fail them.

Ban single-use expanded polypropylene packaging, In October 2023 the government banned expanded polystyrene cups and take away food boxes. Some manufacturers have now started using expanded polypropylene boxes., Expanded polypropylene is sometimes marketed as an eco-friendly alternative to the banned expanded polystyrene. It is not green and it's not eco-friendly. It is used primarily for food on the go so can end up as litter or in general waste litter bins and not recycled. Expanded polypropylene (EPP) is not commonly recycled by most local authorities and it will end up in landfill or EFW. There are far more sustainable alternatives such as plant based packaging.

Increase full-time Carer's Allowance to at least £800 per week, We want the government to pay all full-time carers at least £800 per week. Carers should be valued within society and we think their worth should be reflected in the help and benefits they receive. Carers can receive £83.30 a week, however they must provide care for at least 35 hours a week., The weekly rate for round the clock professional care can be thousands of pounds. There is a massive difference between the carer’s allowance and the amounts charged by private companies. I don't think carers are paid enough to live on. Carers can carry out the same, if not more work, than paid carers, looking after individuals. I feel that the amount they are paid demonstrates the disdain and lack of appreciation that they receive.

Legalise Cannabis recreationally for sale and consumption, We urge the UK government to legalise cannabis by 2025 for medicinal and recreational use (ages 18+), including cultivation, production, and sale under a robust regulatory framework., Legalization will ensure safe, high-quality products, generate significant tax revenue, reduce illegal trade, and provide medical relief for patients. Unlike decriminalization, regulated legalization guarantees consumer safety, supports economic growth, and promotes social unity. Act now to create a safer, healthier, and more prosperous UK.

Grant Malaysian Driving Licence Conversion, We urge the Department for Transport to allow direct conversion of Malaysian driving licences., At present, Malaysians are required to undergo the full GB driving test process (theory and practical), despite Malaysia operating on the same left-hand driving system and having what we think are comparable driving standards.
 
Countries such as Singapore benefit from direct licence conversion agreements with Great Britain. Given what we think are the similar road systems and licensing standards between Malaysia and Singapore, we believe Malaysians should be given the same consideration.

Ban Private Dog Breeding and Strengthen Penalties for Animal Cruelty, We urge the UK Government to ban the private breeding of dogs and allow only registered charities to breed dogs for rehoming. Additionally, we call for stricter minimum sentences for those convicted of animal cruelty, ensuring more consistent punishment and stronger deterrents., We think many animals suffer due to unethical breeding. By restricting breeding to welfare-focused charities and increasing sentencing for abuse, we think we can reduce suffering and promote responsible animal care.

Require political adverts to be truthful & factually accurate, Electoral law doesn’t require claims in political campaigns to be truthful or factually accurate. We think this must change to ensure that citizens can trust what they see broadcast, on billboards or in any written media and to prevent falsehoods swaying votes of the British public., We think the public should be able to trust political parties to present factual information in their campaigns that has documented sources that can be fact checked. The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) holds companies accountable  and we think political parties must be accountable. Following the 1997 General Election, the Committee of Advertising Practice decided to exclude political advertising from the ASA’s remit. We think there needs to be change.
